claims.text: The onset of corrosion degradation in pre-exposure Q235 steel in chloride-rich environments is governed by passive-film formation kinetics.
At approximately 25°C, oxidation is sufficiently slow to form a dense, adherent iron oxide film on Q235 steel.
The dense room-temperature oxide film limits subsequent corrosion of Q235 steel.
At approximately 70°C, rapid oxidation produces a porous, cracked, or otherwise nonprotective oxide film on Q235 steel.
Cracking or spallation of the elevated-temperature oxide film exposes fresh metal and increases the corrosion rate.
Clean, polished Q235 steel with its native oxide removed represents the pre-exposure material state.
A 3.5 wt% NaCl solution is an applicable corrosion-test environment for specimens involving a Q235 steel substrate.
The controlled study varies temperature between approximately 25°C and 70°C while holding chloride concentration, dissolved oxygen, shear, exposure time, and surface preparation constant.
Exposure is conducted for 24–72 hours in static 3.5 wt% NaCl under atmospheric air.
The governing structural mediator is the integrity and morphology of the surface iron oxide film.
Room-temperature samples will form a uniform, adherent passive film and exhibit lower corrosion-current density and minimal mass loss.
Elevated-temperature samples will exhibit higher corrosion-current density, greater mass loss, and more cracked or porous oxide than room-temperature samples.
Changes in chloride concentration or oxygen availability could alter passive-film behavior.
The presence of additional alloying elements could modify passive-film behavior.
Trace Mn in Q235 steel may influence film formation.
Corrosion current, impedance-derived film properties, oxide morphology and composition, oxide thickness, and mass loss can be measured to test the proposed mechanism.
Failure of the 70°C samples to show significantly higher corrosion current, greater mass loss, and a more porous or cracked film than the 25°C samples would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome compares room-temperature samples with an 'untreated baseline,' but the baseline is itself defined as Q235 immersed in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature. Thus, the room-temperature prediction and the stated reference are the same experimental condition rather than distinct groups.

The intervention says dissolved oxygen is held constant while only temperature varies, whereas the conditions specify static solution under atmospheric air and only 'similar' oxygen levels. Atmospheric-equilibrium dissolved oxygen generally varies with temperature unless it is independently controlled.
